title: Three ocean currents meet near the Galapagos
body: The Galapagos lie about 1,000 km west of continental Ecuador. The islands sit where three currents meet, creating a mix of ocean conditions in one location.
takeaway: Land animals face the barrier of a wide ocean, while marine species can reach the same islands along different currents.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Galapagos Islands
visual: a small volcanic island where bands of differently coloured water meet

title: Greenland's Ilulissat Icefjord is an outlet for the ice sheet
body: The Ilulissat Icefjord on western Greenland's coast is the sea outlet of the Sermeq Kujalleq glacier. It is one of the places where ice flowing from the interior reaches the ocean and breaks into icebergs.
takeaway: An iceberg off the coast can carry ice that formed far inland.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ilulissat Icefjord (2004)
visual: towering icebergs packed into a narrow Greenland fjord

title: A protected area in Himachal holds the headwaters of several rivers
body: The Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area covers about 905 square kilometres. It includes upper mountain catchments where glaciers and snow feed several rivers used by communities downstream.
takeaway: Land that looks remote can still be part of the water supply for people well outside the park.
source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Great Himalayan National Park (2014)
